title: Second life: I buy back my own books from second-hand shops
gist: A personal essay on treasure-hunting in second-hand bookshops from Hay-on-Wye to Budapest, Ile de Re, New York and Letchworth, and the author's habit of buying back books he already owned. Light, anecdotal and without market-relevant claims.

insights.claim: Richard Booth opened his first bookshop in Hay-on-Wye in 1961 and built the town into a book capital; it now has about 20 bookshops and hosts the UK's most prestigious annual book festival.
insights.speaker: Vitali Vitaliev
insights.so_what: An example of a niche cultural cluster turning a depressed town into a durable destination economy.
insights.locator: Richard Booth opened his first bookshop

insights.claim: Hay-on-Wye's bookshop has become orderly and fully catalogued, which the author says removes the joy of unexpected discovery that once defined it.
insights.speaker: Vitali Vitaliev
insights.so_what: Curation and professionalisation can trade away the serendipity that attracted collectors.
insights.locator: With the joy of an unexpected discovery gone

insights.claim: Quillet on Ile de Re keeps its 80,000-book stock in pristine condition through an in-house open-plan restoration workshop that customers can watch.
insights.speaker: Vitali Vitaliev
insights.so_what: Restoration-as-theatre is a differentiator for independent bookshops.

insights.claim: A 1937 biography of NYC mayor Fiorello La Guardia bought at the Strand carries a publishers' sticker saying passages were excised after the mayor's objections, showing censorship existed in Depression-era America.
insights.speaker: Vitali Vitaliev
insights.so_what: Old books preserve evidence of historical suppression that digital texts may not.

insights.claim: The author sometimes rebuys books he himself deposited at David's Bookshop, echoing Clive James, who bought books he already owned for the pleasure of carrying them home.
insights.speaker: Vitali Vitaliev
insights.so_what: Collector behaviour is driven by sentiment more than utility, supporting the second-hand market.
insights.quote: for the sheer pleasure of carrying it home.
insights.locator: Here, I have a confession to make
